gc-allocate-uninitialized-array.title: Skip zero initialization for arrays that are fully overwritten
gc-allocate-uninitialized-array.short: Use AllocateUninitializedArray only for buffers that will be completely filled
gc-allocate-uninitialized-array.summary: GC.AllocateUninitializedArray can avoid array initialization work when the caller will overwrite every element before reading it.
gc-allocate-uninitialized-array.why: For large temporary buffers that are immediately and completely filled, it can remove unnecessary zeroing from a measured hot path.
gc-allocate-uninitialized-array.tips: Use it only when every element is definitely written before any read, and benchmark it against ordinary array allocation.

memorycache-stampede-coordination.title: Coordinate cache misses to prevent a cache stampede
memorycache-stampede-coordination.short: Collapse concurrent regeneration of the same expensive key
memorycache-stampede-coordination.summary: When a popular cache entry expires, many concurrent requests can start the same expensive regeneration work at once.
memorycache-stampede-coordination.why: Per-key coordination limits sudden load amplification against databases or downstream services during cache misses.
memorycache-stampede-coordination.tips: Keep coordination scoped per key and design failure, retry, and expiration behavior so a failed regeneration is not retained forever.

unsafe-skipinit-definite-write.title: Use Unsafe.SkipInit only with definite complete writes
unsafe-skipinit-definite-write.short: Write every required field before reading an uninitialized value
unsafe-skipinit-definite-write.summary: Unsafe.SkipInit omits value initialization and requires the caller to guarantee that uninitialized contents are never observed.
unsafe-skipinit-definite-write.why: It can remove initialization work in narrowly measured hot paths, but misuse can expose indeterminate data.
unsafe-skipinit-definite-write.tips: Avoid it in ordinary code and restrict it to cases where complete assignment is obvious and measurement demonstrates a benefit.

dotnet-counters-runtime-diagnostics.title: Inspect live runtime metrics with dotnet-counters
dotnet-counters-runtime-diagnostics.short: Observe GC, ThreadPool, and other counters from a running process
dotnet-counters-runtime-diagnostics.summary: dotnet-counters continuously reads counters such as System.Runtime metrics from a live .NET process.
dotnet-counters-runtime-diagnostics.why: Allocation rate, GC activity, ThreadPool behavior, and related measurements help narrow performance problems using evidence rather than guesses.
dotnet-counters-runtime-diagnostics.tips: Check diagnostic permissions and overhead in production, and interpret trends together with traces and profiles rather than relying on one number.

optionsmonitor-runtime-configuration.title: Handle runtime configuration changes with IOptionsMonitor
optionsmonitor-runtime-configuration.short: Read current options and subscribe to changes in long-lived services
optionsmonitor-runtime-configuration.summary: IOptionsMonitor<T> exposes the current options value and change notifications when reloadable configuration is updated.
optionsmonitor-runtime-configuration.why: It supports long-running services that intentionally apply selected configuration changes without restarting the process.
optionsmonitor-runtime-configuration.tips: Account for callback lifetime and thread safety, and keep settings fixed at startup when changing them mid-operation would be unsafe.

memorymarshal-getreference-span.title: Access a Span's first reference with MemoryMarshal.GetReference
memorymarshal-getreference-span.short: Bridge Span data to low-level ref-based operations
memorymarshal-getreference-span.summary: MemoryMarshal.GetReference obtains a reference to the first location represented by a Span or ReadOnlySpan.
memorymarshal-getreference-span.why: It can connect bounds-aware Span code to advanced interop or memory routines that operate on references.
memorymarshal-getreference-span.tips: An empty Span can still produce a reference value, but it must not be dereferenced; prefer safe Span APIs in ordinary code.

unix-domain-socket-local-ipc.title: Use Unix domain sockets for local IPC
unix-domain-socket-local-ipc.short: Connect local processes with Socket without exposing a TCP port
unix-domain-socket-local-ipc.summary: UnixDomainSocketEndPoint represents local socket endpoints identified by a filesystem path on supported Unix-like platforms.
unix-domain-socket-local-ipc.why: Local services can communicate with the familiar Socket stream model without publishing a network-facing TCP port.
unix-domain-socket-local-ipc.tips: Check platform support and design cleanup for both socket lifetime and any filesystem socket path left behind.

partitioned-rate-limiter-fairness.title: Partition rate limits by user or key
partitioned-rate-limiter-fairness.short: Apply independent quotas instead of one shared global limit
partitioned-rate-limiter-fairness.summary: PartitionedRateLimiter selects an independent RateLimiter from a partition key such as a user or API key.
partitioned-rate-limiter-fairness.why: Partitioning prevents one high-volume caller from consuming the entire shared allowance and lets applications define fairness explicitly.
partitioned-rate-limiter-fairness.tips: Avoid an unbounded number of partition keys and define a deliberate key strategy for anonymous or unauthenticated requests.

semaphoreslim-release-balance.title: Balance SemaphoreSlim waits and releases
semaphoreslim-release-balance.short: Release a permit only after acquisition actually succeeded
semaphoreslim-release-balance.summary: If WaitAsync is canceled or fails before acquiring a permit, an unconditional Release can incorrectly increase the semaphore count.
semaphoreslim-release-balance.why: Tracking successful acquisition prevents concurrency limits from silently drifting and allowing more work than intended.
semaphoreslim-release-balance.tips: Structure code so Release follows only a successful WaitAsync, and also guard against releases beyond the configured maximum.

arraypool-clear-sensitive-data.title: Do not return sensitive data to ArrayPool uncleared
arraypool-clear-sensitive-data.short: Erase secrets before returning shared pooled buffers
arraypool-clear-sensitive-data.summary: Arrays returned to ArrayPool may later be rented by other code, so secret material can remain in reused storage if it is not cleared.
arraypool-clear-sensitive-data.why: Clearing buffers that contain keys or credentials reduces unintended data retention across pool reuse.
arraypool-clear-sensitive-data.tips: Consider the performance cost and the exact sensitive range, and minimize the lifetime of secret data even when clearArray is used.
